Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import json
def f(G):
    H=len(G); W=len(G[0])
    import collections
    cnt=collections.Counter(x for r in G for x in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # find the object(s): contiguous non-bg non-marker groups
    # objects = connected components of non-bg values
    seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    objs=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if G[i][j]!=bg and not seen[i][j]:
                stack=[(i,j)]; comp=[]
                while stack:
                    y,x=stack.pop()
                    if seen[y][x]: continue
                    seen[y][x]=True; comp.append((y,x))
                    for dy in(-1,0,1):
                        for dx in(-1,0,1):
                            ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                            if 0<=ny<H and 0<=nx<W and G[ny][nx]!=bg and not seen[ny][nx]:
                                stack.append((ny,nx))
                objs.append(comp)
    out=[r[:] for r in G]
    # pick largest component as object
    big=max(objs,key=len)
    ys=[y for y,x in big]; xs=[x for y,x in big]
    y0,y1=min(ys),max(ys); x0,x1=min(xs),max(xs)
    h=y1-y0+1; w=x1-x0+1
    sub=[[G[y][x] for x in range(x0,x1+1)] for y in range(y0,y1+1)]
    # noise points: isolated single cells of any non-bg color
    pts=[(i,j,G[i][j]) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if G[i][j]!=bg and (i,j) not in set(big)]
    for y,x,v in pts:
        rel=(y-y0,x-x0)
        if 0<=rel[0]<h and 0<=rel[1]<w:
            out[y][x]=sub[rel[0]][rel[1]]
    return out
d=G['Demo pair 1 input']; exp=G['Demo pair 1 output']
print(f(d)==exp)
out=f(G['Test input'])
for r in out: print(r)

def f(G):

    cnt={}
    for r in G:
        for x in r: cnt[x]=cnt.get(x,0)+1
    bg=max(cnt,key=lambda k:cnt[k])
    seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]; comps=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if G[i][j]!=bg and not seen[i][j]:
                st=[(i,j)]; comp=set()
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop()
                    if seen[y][x] or G[y][x]==bg: continue
                    seen[y][x]=True; comp.add((y,x))
                    for dy in(-1,0,1):

                            if 0<=ny<H and 0<=nx<W and not seen[ny][nx]:

    big=max(comps,key=len)
    ys=[p[0] for p in big]; xs=[p[1] for p in big]
    y0,y1,x0,x1=min(ys),max(ys),min(xs),max(xs)
    sub=[[G[y][x] for x in range(x0,x1+1)] for y in range(y0,y1+1)]
    h,w=len(sub),len(sub[0])
    out=[r[:] for r in G]
    # noise cells = other components
    others=[c for c in comps if c!=big]
    pts=[(y,x,G[y][x]) for c in others for y,x in c]
    # direction: if noise in same row as some object cell -> horizontal? demo noise vertical pair (col0 rows14,15)->cols7,8 (top of obj)
